Matchstick 1.5 Installer Manual

Matchstick gives Savant IP control of Amazon Fire TV devices: navigation, apps, power, Live TV, and, with the Keyboard profile, the Savant Pro app's text entry and pairing.

Savant (profile)  --TCP 2360-->  Matchstick on the Savant host  --ADB 5555-->  Fire TV

A Fire TV's only network control method is ADB (Android Debug Bridge), which Savant can't speak. Matchstick is a small service on the Savant host that speaks ADB to each Fire TV, and the Matchstick profile in Blueprint talks to that service over plain TCP. One service serves every Fire TV in the home.

1. Before you start

Supported Fire TVs (Fire OS, which has ADB):

WorksDoes NOT work (Vega OS, no ADB)
Fire TV Stick 4K, 4K Max, 4K PlusFire TV Stick 4K Select (2025)
Fire TV Cube (all generations)Fire TV Stick HD (2026) and newer sticks
Fire TV built-in TVs (Omni, Insignia, Toshiba)

Spec a Fire TV Cube or a 4K Max on Savant jobs. A wired connection (the Cube's Ethernet port, or an Ethernet adapter for a stick) is the most reliable.

You need:

  • The Savant host (Mac mini) on the same network as the Fire TVs, and the Savant user's password.
  • Internet on the host during install (to download Android platform-tools), or the file platform-tools-latest-darwin.zip from Google placed next to install.sh.
  • Physical access to each Fire TV and its remote, once, to approve pairing.
  • A DHCP reservation for each Fire TV.

2. Prepare each Fire TV

  1. Settings → My Fire TV → Developer Options → ADB debugging: ON. If Developer Options is missing: Settings → My Fire TV → About, select the device name seven times, then go back.
  2. Note its IP address (Settings → My Fire TV → About → Network) and reserve it in the router.

3. Install on the Savant host

  1. Copy the matchstick folder to the host (for example into Downloads).

  2. In Terminal on the host, as the Savant user, not with sudo:

    bash ~/Downloads/matchstick/install.sh

    This installs to ~/matchstick. To use another folder: bash install.sh ~/some-folder.

  3. Enter the Savant user's password when asked. It's needed once, to install the service and to add the firetvctl shortcut in /usr/local/bin.

The installer finishes with Matchstick 1.5.1 installed and running on port 2360.

What it installs:

  • ~/matchstick/: the bridge, config, logs, adb, the key helper and firetvctl.
  • /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.matchstick.bridge.plist: a system service that runs as the Savant user, starts at boot and restarts itself if it stops.
  • /usr/local/bin/firetvctl: a shortcut to ~/matchstick/firetvctl.

Why a system service? macOS 15's Local Network privacy blocks login items from reaching devices on the LAN; adb connect then fails with "No route to host" although ping works. System services aren't affected.

4. Pair each Fire TV

On the host:

firetvctl pair 192.168.1.50

On the TV, Allow USB debugging? appears. Tick Always allow from this computer, then choose OK. The command prints Paired. Model: ....

Check it:

firetvctl test 192.168.1.50 HOME

The TV goes to the home screen.

Pairing is stored on the Fire TV and survives reboots. A factory reset clears it; pair again.

5. Choose a profile

Both profiles are in profile/blueprint-import/. Use one per Fire TV.

Amazon Fire TV (Matchstick)Amazon Fire TV (Matchstick Keyboard)
Fileamazon_fire tv (matchstick).xmlamazon_fire tv (matchstick keyboard).xml
Savant serviceFire TV (media server)Apple TV service (rebranded to Fire TV, section 7)
Pro app text pop-upNo (TypeText action only)Yes
Pairing from the Pro appNoYes (Settings → Devices)
TV button double press → Live TVNo (LiveTV custom action)Yes
Remote buttonsFull standard media remoteApple TV style remote; extra buttons as custom actions

Pick Keyboard when clients will search and type in apps. Pick the standard profile for the fullest standard remote.

6. Set up in Blueprint

  1. Import the profile into Blueprint's library from profile/blueprint-import/. Each profile there sits with its two companions, all with the same name:

    FileWhat
    amazon_fire tv (matchstick).xmlThe profile
    amazon_fire tv (matchstick).htmThis manual, for the component's Documentation tab
    amazon_fire tv (matchstick).icnsThe component icon

    (The same three for the Keyboard profile, amazon_fire tv (matchstick keyboard).) Importing the .xml brings in the .htm and .icns from the same folder, and Blueprint files them into its library itself. Keep the three together and don't rename any of them: Blueprint matches them by the profile's file name, <manufacturer>_<model> in lower case. A renamed profile still shows in the component list, but dragging it in fails with "Component not found".

  2. Add the component to the design, one per Fire TV.
  3. Control port: wire the component's ETHERNET port to your network switch. The Device IP Address field then appears under Control Ports. Set it to the Savant host's IP, or 127.0.0.1 since Matchstick runs on the host (it listens on port 2360).
  4. Inspector → State Variables → Fire TV IP Address: the Fire TV's own IP.
  5. Wire the HDMI output like any source.

Every Fire TV component uses the same host IP. The Fire TV IP Address state variable tells Matchstick which Fire TV each command is for.

7. Keyboard profile: Pro app setup

Rebrand the service. The Pro app shows this profile as Apple TV. To make it look like a Fire TV:

  • In the service icon settings, set Brand to Display to Amazon Fire TV.
  • In the service order list, set an alias (for example FireTV) for the group and each component.

The profile sets the service's UI Mapping to atv-bridge itself (Service Preferences table); nothing to change there.

The result: the Fire TV logo on the home screen, with your alias as its label.

Text entry. When a text box is on the Fire TV screen (search, or an app's keyboard), the Pro app shows its text pop-up. What's typed there replaces the box contents and is submitted; on the Fire TV search screen this opens the results.

Pairing. The Fire TV appears under Settings → Devices → Apple TV in the Pro app.

  • Pair shows Allow USB debugging? on the TV for a Fire TV that isn't paired yet. There is no PIN: approve on the TV; any PIN the app asks for is ignored.
  • Unpair is ignored on purpose (it's logged), so a stray tap can't cut off control. To really disconnect a Fire TV, remove it from the design or turn off ADB debugging on it.

TV button. The app's TV button is Home. Press it twice quickly (within 0.6 s) for the Double Home Action, set per component under Inspector → State Variables:

Double Home ActionDouble press does
livetv (default)Opens the Live TV channel guide
offNothing extra (just Home)
an app alias or package, e.g. netflix, com.hulu.plusOpens that app
key:<android keycode>, e.g. key:172Sends that key

A single press goes Home immediately; the double press is never slower.

Remote layout. The Apple TV service has fewer buttons: Menu is the Fire TV Back button. Back, Stop, Scan, Skip and Setup are available as custom actions.

8. Buttons, actions and states

Standard profile service buttons: PowerOn/Off, Home, Select, OSD cursor, Play/Pause (a toggle, like the Fire TV remote), Stop, ScanUp/ScanDown (fast forward/rewind), SkipUp/SkipDown, Exit/Back, Menu/Info (options), Setup (Fire TV Settings).

Custom actions (both profiles), for buttons and workflows:

ActionDoes
PowerToggle, PlayOnly, PauseOnlyDiscrete power/play/pause
VolumeUp, VolumeDown, MuteToggleSent to the TV/AVR over HDMI-CEC (normally route volume to the AVR/TV in Savant)
SearchOpens Fire TV search
LiveTVOpens the Live TV channel guide
EnterSubmits typed text; on the search screen opens the results
HomeLongPressLong-press Home (quick settings and sleep menu)
LaunchAppOpens an app by alias or Android package name
TypeTextTypes text into the focused text box
Netflix, PrimeVideo, YouTube, YouTubeTV, DisneyPlus, Hulu, Max, AppleTV, ParamountPlus, Peacock, Plex, PlutoTV, SlingTV, Spotify, Kodi, SettingsOne-touch app launch
Refresh, RequestAllStatesRefresh status now, or resend every value

App aliases for LaunchApp: appletv, disneyplus, hulu, kodi, max, netflix, paramountplus, peacock, plex, pluto, primevideo, settings, sling, spotify, youtube, youtubetv. For any other app, find its package with firetvctl apps <ip> and use the package name, or add an alias (section 10).

States (for feedback and conditions):

StateValues
ONLINE1 when Matchstick can control the Fire TV. Gate automations on this.
ADBCONNECTED, UNAUTHORIZED (approve on the TV) or OFFLINE
POWERON or OFF (asleep)
APP_NAME, APP_PACKAGEThe app in front, e.g. Netflix / com.netflix.ninja
PLAYBACKPLAYING, PAUSED or STOPPED
MODEL, FIREOSFire TV model code and Fire OS version
LAST_ERRORBlank, or what went wrong and what to do
BRIDGE_VERSIONMatchstick version
KeyboardFocused, PairingState, PairingError, Discovered, AvailableAppsKeyboard profile only: the Apple TV service states the Pro app uses

Known limits: on Fire OS 6, Fire TV Settings reports APP_NAME as Home. On Fire OS 8, Search opens the search tab by moving to it (about 4 seconds), and the Pro app keyboard only pops up when search was opened from Savant, not with the Fire TV remote. Status refreshes every 5 seconds and about 1 second after each command.

What working feedback looks like. Savant's State Values window, filtered on the component name, shows every state Matchstick reports. A healthy Fire TV reads ONLINE 1, ADB CONNECTED and a blank LAST_ERROR, with the app in front in APP_NAME and APP_PACKAGE. Use these for feedback on buttons and custom screens, and as conditions in workflows (for example, only send a command when ONLINE is 1, or start a lighting scene when APP_NAME is Netflix).

Standard profile: the Fire TV's states, plus Savant's volume and mute states for the zone.

Keyboard profile: the same Fire TV states, plus the Apple TV service states the Pro app uses (KeyboardFocused, PairingState, Discovered).

Two components can point at the same Fire TV, as here; both get the same Fire TV states. Only the component the zone is using shows ServiceIsActive 1.

9. firetvctl

Run on the host. start, stop and restart ask for the Savant user's password.

CommandDoes
firetvctl statusIs it running and answering; which Fire TVs are paired
firetvctl start / stop / restartControl the service
firetvctl logsFollow the log (Ctrl-C to stop)
firetvctl pair <ip>Approve this host on a Fire TV
firetvctl apps <ip>List installed app package names
firetvctl test <ip> <COMMAND> [arg]Send a command, e.g. firetvctl test 192.168.1.50 LAUNCH netflix
firetvctl versionMatchstick version

The IP comes first: firetvctl test 192.168.1.50 LAUNCH netflix, not firetvctl test netflix ....

Every command Matchstick receives is logged with the sender's port, so firetvctl logs shows what Savant sent and when (routine status polls are left out).

Test scripts in tools/, for troubleshooting on site. On a host with Matchstick installed they use the running service; elsewhere they start a temporary bridge.

ScriptDoes
bash tools/adb_test.sh <ip>Full check: pairing, keys, apps, Settings, sleep and wake
bash tools/keyboard_test.sh <ip>Keyboard profile commands: text entry, clear, app list, pairing
bash tools/keys_test.sh <ip>Navigation keys with pauses to watch the TV
bash tools/grid_walk.sh <ip>, fast_walk.sh <ip>Move around a grid, slowly or quickly
bash tools/launch_settings.sh <ip>Opens Fire TV Settings and watches status
bash tools/send.sh <ip> "CMD [arg]" ...Send any commands and print what comes back

10. Configuration

~/matchstick/config.json. After editing, run firetvctl restart.

SettingDefaultMeaning
listen_port2360Port Savant connects to
poll_seconds5Status refresh while Savant is connected
idle_disconnect_minutes30Drop ADB to a Fire TV nobody has used for this long
allowed_devices[] (any LAN address)Lock Matchstick to these Fire TV IPs
allowed_clients[] (anyone on the LAN)Only accept connections from these IPs
app_aliases{}Extra app names, e.g. {"tubi": "com.tubitv"}
live_tvkey:172What LiveTV opens: key:<keycode> or an app alias/package
home_double_press_seconds0.6Double-press window for Home; 0 turns it off everywhere
stall_hold_seconds600How long to wait for a Fire TV that stops answering before reconnecting
relay_base_port20000First local port for the per-Fire TV ADB relays (host only, 127.0.0.1)
log_levelINFODEBUG logs every status poll too

11. Troubleshooting

Start with firetvctl status and firetvctl logs. LAST_ERROR in Savant usually says what to do.

SymptomCause and fix
firetvctl: command not foundYou're on another computer, or the shortcut was skipped. Use ~/matchstick/firetvctl.
"No route to host" pairing, though ping worksOld install running as a login item: re-run install.sh (1.2 and later install a system service).
Pairing says unauthorized, no prompt on the TVWake the TV and stay on its input. Turn ADB debugging off and on, then firetvctl pair again.
LAST_ERROR "Fire TV not answering (asleep or off Wi-Fi?) - waiting for it"Normal with the TV off: the Fire TV goes quiet on Wi-Fi for a few seconds every few minutes. Matchstick holds the connection and carries on when it answers, usually within 20 s. Commands sent meanwhile are dropped; send them again.
ADB stays OFFLINE (log shows "shell lost"; adb devices shows the Fire TV as offline)The Fire TV is holding an old ADB connection and refusing new ones. 1.4.1 prevents the usual cause and clears it by itself (LAST_ERROR "Fire TV is holding an old ADB connection - clearing it"). If it stays offline, turn ADB debugging off and on, or restart the Fire TV (a Savant-controlled power outlet can automate this). Note the time in the log for support.
IP netflix not allowedArguments in the wrong order. The Fire TV IP comes first.
Can't drag the profile into Blueprint ("Component not found")The file was renamed. Use the original file name.
No Device IP Address field in BlueprintWire the ETHERNET port to the network switch first.
Documentation tab greyed out on the componentThe profile was imported without its .htm beside it (copied in by hand, renamed, or from another folder). Import it again from profile/blueprint-import/ (section 6). Or copy <profile name>.htm into the documentation folder of your custom profiles folder, then close and reopen the component's documentation.
Component shows a "?" instead of the Fire TV iconThe profile was imported without its .icns beside it, or the component was added before the icon was in the library; each design keeps its own copy. Import again from profile/blueprint-import/ for new components. Copy the icon into the design's images folder (inside the saved .rpmConfig) named like the profile with an upper-case .ICNS, e.g. amazon_fire tv (matchstick).ICNS, then close and reopen the design. Or remove the component and add it again.
Keys feel slowfiretvctl logs should show key helper running after each connect. If it says the helper didn't start, keys fall back to slower methods; restart the service.
CEC didn't turn the TV onFire TV PowerOn wakes the Fire TV; turn the TV on from Savant as usual.
App launch shows "not installed"Check the package with firetvctl apps <ip>.
Pro app text pop-up doesn't appearOnly the Keyboard profile has it. The box must be on screen (KeyboardFocused true).

Speed. Key presses take about 0.05 s. Matchstick keeps a small helper running on each Fire TV (/data/local/tmp/matchstick-keys.dex) so no program starts per press. If it isn't running, keys fall back to the physical remote's input device (while the remote is connected), then to Android's input command (0.3 to 1.2 s per press).

Sleep. A Fire TV goes to sleep when the TV turns off (HDMI-CEC). Matchstick stays connected, and PowerOn wakes it. While asleep it goes quiet on Wi-Fi for a few seconds every few minutes; Matchstick waits these out. If a unit keeps dropping off the network for longer, put it on Ethernet.

ADB relay. adb on the host reaches each Fire TV through a small relay inside Matchstick (127.0.0.1, from port 20000), which holds the Fire TV's one ADB connection through quiet spells. firetvctl status shows it next to the IP. To use adb by hand while the service runs, go through firetvctl (pair, apps, test); connecting straight to <ip>:5555 from another computer is refused while Matchstick holds the connection.

12. Upgrade and uninstall

Upgrade: copy the new matchstick folder to the host and run its install.sh with the same folder as before (for example bash install.sh or bash install.sh ~/adb-test). Pairings, config.json and logs are kept. Then import the new profiles into Blueprint from profile/blueprint-import/ and refresh the components. Blueprint only updates a component when the profile's version is higher than the one in the design (this release is profile version 1.5). Upgrading from 1.1 or earlier also replaces the old login item with the system service.

Uninstall:

bash ~/matchstick/uninstall.sh            # add --keep-config to save config.json first

It removes only what the installer created, and asks for the password to remove the service and the shortcut. Nothing in Savant is touched. The key helper file on each Fire TV (/data/local/tmp/matchstick-keys.dex, 3 KB) is left; it's removed by a factory reset, and it does nothing on its own.

13. Security

ADB gives full control of a Fire TV, so:

  • Matchstick only accepts its fixed list of commands, and only for private (LAN) addresses.
  • Lock it down further with allowed_devices and allowed_clients (section 10).
  • Approving pairing on a Fire TV trusts this host's ADB key (stored in the Savant user's ~/.android). Keep the host secure, and don't approve pairing prompts you didn't start.
